thread:
maya: heads up — noticed a weird drop in the conversion funnel this morning. TOF traffic is up ~18% but MQL -> SQL conversion fell ~30% overnight. anyone else seeing this on the pulseboard?

leo: saw the spike, digging into UTM breakdown now. looks like a lot of traffic from the blog post (paid social tag `utm_medium=social`) but conversion rate from that cohort is low.

sam: tagging the lead-routing team — could routing rules be throttling or misclassifying some MQLs? @olivia any recent changes to routing?

olivia: we pushed a small rule tweak last night to prioritize enterprise leads by `company_size` because of a spike in demo requests. didn't touch MQL criteria. will check the logs.

analytics-bot: dashboard update: funnel_v2 | TOF 92,341 (+18%) | MQL 3,200 (-30%) | SQL 1,240 (-28%) — 2034567890 06:12 UTC

maya: thanks — can someone pull a sample of ~200 leads from the affected cohort (blog/social) with full UTM, lead_source, routing_decision fields? need to confirm if they were tagged as MQL or filtered by routing.

leo: running SQL now, quick snippet I'm using:
```sql
SELECT id, created_at, utm_source, utm_medium, lead_source, mql_flag, routing_queue
FROM leads
WHERE created_at >= '2024-10-12' AND utm_medium = 'social'
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 200;
```

sam: FYI we saw ~12% sample-rate drop on the inbound webhook last night (instrumentation sidecar restarted during deploy). that could explain missing MQL events. opening a ticket.

natalie: if sample-rate changed that would affect attribution too — our weekly KPI decks assume full event coverage. we should flag potential undercount in Friday review.

olivia: checked routing logs — none of the blog/social cohort were sent to the enterprise queue. routing decisions look normal. I'm forwarding a 1-hour log slice to the thread.

maya: good. sam — what's ETA on the ticket? need root cause before we call it an attribution artifact.

sam: ticket #MK-534 opened, root cause looks like a flaky consumer on the event pipeline (consumer restart caused 15-20% loss for ~40m). ETA for full fix: 6 hours, hotfix in 2.

leo: adding a temporary correction layer to the dashboard to show "event ingestion health" so we can annotate the timeline. will push a note to the pulseboard.

analytics-bot: note added: "ingestion anomaly detected 2024-10-12 01:12-01:52 UTC —counts may be underreported" — 2034567925 06:22 UTC

natalie: ok let's be conservative in the weekly numbers. I'll add a slide to the Friday KPI deck: call out the ingestion gap, show adjusted vs raw MQL/SQL, and propose to exclude that window from trend calculations.

maya: also want a quick attribution sanity check — if last-touch attribution overweights blog/social this week, conversion efficiency metrics will be misleading. can we include both last-touch and multi-touch results on the slide?

leo: yes. pulling both attribution models now. quick note: multi-touch reduces the blog line by ~9% vs last-touch.

sam: hotfix applied to consumer, replay started. will run a reconciliation job overnight to recover lost events.

olivia: routing audit complete — no misrouted leads. will add audit CSV to the ticket.

maya: action items: 1) sam to confirm replay success and provide final reconciliation numbers (owner: sam) 2) leo to surface ingestion health annotation + both attribution models on the dashboard (owner: leo) 3) natalie to update Friday deck with adjusted figures and callouts (owner: natalie) 4) olivia to attach routing audit (owner: olivia). please comment when done. :white_check_mark:

sam: reconciliation queued, will post results here when finished (ETA 12h).

leo: pushed dashboard annotation and added multi-touch toggle. link: https://pulse.redwood.ai/dashboards/funnels (internal)

natalie: draft slide added to deck: "Oct 12 ingestion gap — effect on MQL->SQL". marked as draft for review.

maya: great. once reconciliation is in, we'll validate numbers and decide whether to exclude the window from month-over-month. thanks team. :pray:
